Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
  SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
  SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
  SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
  SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
  SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
  SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
  SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
  SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
  SPA-N-014: Category separation
  SPA-N-015: Title verification
  SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms

**Scope note:** The Seller's "reviewer efficiency note" says [STANDARD] items have been cleared and need no scrutiny. I haven't relied on it. Several [STANDARD] items (the disclosure, buyer-knowledge, and limitation clauses) carry material exposure, and the Seller's disclosure letter reserves its position on all of them. Items SPA-N-005, N-014 and N-015 are not expressly addressed in the Seller's pack, so I've flagged them as buyer-side gaps.

**Priority items:** SPA-N-009 (Riverlark payoff), SPA-N-012 (privacy notification clock), SPA-N-008 (Bluefen consent), SPA-N-011 (Ironquay IP), SPA-N-010 (bonuses in the price), and SPA-N-006/007 (disclosure and buyer knowledge).

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Aggregate general warranty liability capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8M).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher general cap (open at 30%, AUD 7.2M; fallback about 25%). Fundamental, tax, and specific indemnities sit outside the general cap. Fraud is uncapped.
- **Recommendation:** Counter. Reject 20% as the opening position.
- **Reason:** A 20% cap leaves the buyer carrying most of the gap on a deal where known issues total well over AUD 4.8M in exposure.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** Claims under AUD 25,000 are not actionable. A deductible basket of AUD 250,000 applies, so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** A lower de minimis (around AUD 10,000), with related claims aggregated. A "tipping" basket, so that once it is exceeded the claim is recovered from the first dollar. Basket and de minimis do not apply to fundamental, tax, or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a tipping basket and reduced de minimis.
- **Reason:** A deductible basket absorbs the first AUD 250,000 of loss (about 1% of price) and could bar a large share of smaller warranty claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** General claims must be notified within 18 months of Completion, and any limitation applies to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** General warranties at 36 months (fallback 24). Fundamental and tax claims at 6–7 years or the statutory limitation period plus a buffer. Specific indemnities run until resolved.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 18 months.
- **Reason:** Bluefen, Ironquay, and privacy exposures may not surface within 18 months, especially across a full audit cycle.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the general cap and time limit "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title to shares, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, with no basket or de minimis and a 6-year period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject.
- **Reason:** Title to the shares is the core asset. Capping it at 20% would leave the buyer exposed on 80% of its purchase price if title fails.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (not addressed by Seller)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy, and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (9.3, 12.8, 20.5). No fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that nothing in the limitation, exclusive-remedy, or non-reliance provisions limits liability for fraud. Preserve any statutory misleading-conduct claims that cannot be excluded. Australian counsel should confirm the enforceability of the non-reliance wording.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out.
- **Reason:** Without it, the drafting could be read to cover the Seller's own fraud, which a contract cannot safely exclude.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Clause 1.1 discloses everything in the data room (DD-002 to DD-012). Clause 1.2 discloses accounts, statutory registers, and public searches. Schedule 7 relies on general disclosure.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, against specific warranties, with fair-disclosure standards. Data room and public-register general disclosure rejected. Accounts disclosed only against the relevant accounts warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure.
- **Reason:** Disclosing the whole data room would neutralise the warranty package, since almost any warranty breach could be argued to be disclosed.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete 8.3. Insert a clear pro-sandbagging clause so that buyer knowledge does not affect warranty claims. Specific indemnities apply regardless of knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Reject, and insert pro-sandbagging wording.
- **Reason:** The buyer already knows of DD-002 to DD-012 issues. Clause 8.3 would bar warranty claims for exactly those issues, so they must be dealt with through specific indemnities or price.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent, treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent is in the data room, and conditions in clause 11.3 are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** Written consent plus satisfaction of the clause 11.3 conditions as a condition precedent, not on a reasonable-endeavours basis. No waiver without buyer agreement. If not obtained, the buyer may walk away or obtain a price adjustment or escrow. Specific indemnity for loss of Bluefen revenue if the contract terminates after a change of control within a set period.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a condition precedent.
- **Reason:** About AUD 3.6M (roughly 30%) of FY26 revenue depends on a consent that is unverified and conditional.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2M outstanding, with a release to be provided "following Completion."
- **Buyer wants:** Payoff at Completion from the purchase price, consistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis. Obtain a payoff letter, discharge of security (including PPSR), and a waiver of the clause 8.1 change-control. The funds flow should pay Riverlark directly.
- **Recommendation:** Require payoff and discharge at Completion.
- **Reason:** A post-Completion release leaves AUD 3.2M of debt and security sitting in a company the buyer now owns, which contradicts the debt-free price mechanics.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** Treat the bonuses as a seller-borne transaction or debt-like item, deducted from price or paid by the seller. Include employer on-costs. Indicatively, superannuation at 12% and NSW payroll tax (5.45%) could bring the total to about AUD 0.49M if all apply. Confirm with a payroll adviser. Specific indemnity for any bonus claims.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct from price and include on-costs.
- **Reason:** The amount sits outside the funds flow and would otherwise pass to the buyer after Completion.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW 3 payment, described as "adequate."
- **Buyer wants:** An indemnity covering all Ironquay claims and IP title. Scope matched to clause 7.3, which conditions transfer on payment of every SOW 3 fee, not just one payment. Seller to pay the AUD 180,000 open amount before Completion or have it deducted. Bank evidence of payment. A confirmatory assignment of Project Materials as a condition precedent. Separate cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Require a broader indemnity and pre-Completion settlement.
- **Reason:** The IP may not transfer to the company if SOW 3 fees remain unpaid, and DD-010 is not bank verification.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material."
- **Buyer wants:** Reject that characterisation. Require an immediate forensic investigation covering access logs and scope. Assess whether the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme under Part IIIC of the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies. The company's turnover appears to exceed the AUD 3M threshold given FY26 revenue of about AUD 12M, so the Act is likely to apply. The 30-day assessment period runs from when the company had reasonable grounds to suspect an eligible breach, so the buyer should confirm when that was. Seller to bear costs. Specific indemnity for regulatory, notification, remediation, and third-party claims, outside basket and de minimis, with a separate cap and a longer time limit. Data-security warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Specific indemnity and a pre-Completion investigation.
- **Reason:** About 1,240 personal records may have been exposed, access is unknown, and the statutory notification clock may already be running.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** Review the terms (term, termination rights, auto-renewal, escalators). Interim covenant that no renewals occur without buyer consent. Seller bears any pre-Completion cost or termination charge. Confirm the ordinary-course characterisation before accepting it.
- **Recommendation:** Require buyer consent and review of the terms.
- **Reason:** The three renewals are related, may be timed to shift costs to the buyer, and the Seller has not said whether they are terminable or accrued.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation (not addressed by Seller)
- **Seller:** A single regime applies to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories, each with its own cap, basket, and time limit: (a) general warranties; (b) fundamental; (c) tax; (d) IP; (e) specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Bluefen, Riverlark). Specific indemnities sit outside basket and de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime.
- **Reason:** Under one regime, known specific risks would be capped at the general level and cut off at 18 months.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (not addressed by Seller)
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. Nothing is said about buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent ASIC current and historical company extracts. Inspection of the original register. PPSR searches for encumbrances. Seller warranties on title, capacity, and no encumbrances. Signed share transfer and certificates delivered at Completion. Fundamental indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Verify independently before signing.
- **Reason:** The register is seller-supplied and does not confirm that the buyer will receive clean title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Specific tax indemnity for pre-Completion taxes (income tax, GST, payroll tax, superannuation, FBT), with a separate cap and a statutory-limitation-based time limit. Tax warranties. IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement, and contractor assignments, with a separate cap and a longer period. Neither sits within the general basket.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept as settled. Negotiate separate tax and IP regimes.
- **Reason:** Under the general regime, pre-Completion tax exposure would face the 20% cap and 18-month limit, and no part of it has been agreed.

---

*This is an AI-generated first-pass review, not legal advice. The figures are taken from the Seller's documents and have not been independently verified. Australian counsel should review the enforceability of the non-reliance, fraud, and sandbagging wording, the Privacy Act notification analysis, and the payroll-tax and superannuation estimates before positions are sent.*
